newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian parliament to discuss budget.
newsitem.headline: Indian parliament to discuss budget.

text.p: India's parliament begins budget discussions on Wednesday after new Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition was boosted by a key ex-minister's move to join the government.

Former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party's decision to join the government, rocked by a corruption scandal, has paved the way for Gujral to bring Chidambaram into the cabinet.
Chidambaram, an outspoken advocate of free-market reforms, was expected to be sworn in as the finance minister to pilot the pathbreaking 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget in parliament.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma will induct new members of Gujral's cabinet on Wednesday evening at 7.30 p.m. (1400 GMT), a presidential spokesman told Reuters.
He did not say how many ministers would take oath of office in the ceremony, nor who they would be.

"He (Chidambaram) is a certainty," a government official told Reuters when asked if Chidambaram, finance minister in the ousted government of former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, would return to his post.

"Chidambaram's return will reinforce the confidence of industry and investors and also help restore India's international image," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted a spokesperson for the Confederation of Indian Industry as saying.
Parliament will take up the 1997/98 budget for discussion during the week and is expected to put it to vote in the Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament, next month.
The budget session of parliament is expected to continue until May 16.
The Congress party, which provides crucial make-or-break support to Gujral's government, announced on Tuesday it would not allow Gujral's government to fall in a budget vote.
Congress had provoked Gujral's predecessor Deve Gowda's fall by withdrawing its vital support in parliament.

But Gujral's government was likely to face attack from the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which is expected to raise the issue of a corruption scandal and has pledged to move amendments in the budget proposals.

Federal police on Sunday said they would prosecute Laloo Prasad Yadav, president of Gujral's Janata Dal party and chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, and 55 others in a $280 million corruption case.
The federal police will also prosecute Chandradeo Prasad Varma, a junior Rural Areas and Employment minister in Gujral's council of ministers.
The scandal, stretching back more than a decade but uncovered last year, involved the alleged misuse of funds for an animal welfare scheme.
BJP will demand the resignation of Laloo and Varma, party officials said.
